name: Socialism with Chinese characteristics
summary: Socialism with Chinese characteristics is the Chinese Communist Party’s official doctrine since Deng Xiaoping: China is in the primary stage of socialism, so it keeps public ownership as the mainstay alongside a socialist market economy, opens to foreign investment, and puts the Party in overall leadership of the state, the army and society. Its constitutions pair a people’s democratic dictatorship led by the working class with people’s congresses, regional ethnic autonomy and One Country, Two Systems, and reject Western separation of powers.
scope: The doctrine as the Party and PRC constitutions state it (the Article 1 formula of the PRC Constitution; the Party Constitution’s General Program), Deng Xiaoping’s founding speeches of 1979 and 1992, the 2021 Resolution on the Party’s history and the 20th Congress report, as the scholarship of Miller, Goodman and the ASAA brief places them. It excludes Mao Zedong Thought as a separate doctrine and other countries’ socialisms.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The PRC Constitution (Art. 29) sets the armed forces the task of strengthening national defence, and the report calls for building a world-class military.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: The PRC Constitution (Art. 10) makes urban land state-owned but rural land collectively owned.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The PRC Constitution (Art. 36) says no State organ, social group or individual may compel citizens to believe in, or not to believe in, any religion, or discriminate against them for it.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The Party Constitution's principle of mutual noninterference in internal affairs rules out arming insurgents against other governments.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The PRC Constitution (Art. 62) has the National People's Congress review and approve the state budget.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The Party Constitution and the PRC Constitution preamble say class struggle will continue to exist within certain bounds for a long time, though it is no longer the principal contradiction.

conscription.rationale: The PRC Constitution (Art. 55) makes it the honorable duty of citizens to perform military service and join the militia in accordance with law.

defeat-communism.rationale: The ruling Party's Constitution makes communism its highest ideal and ultimate goal.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The Party Constitution commits to oppose hegemonism and power politics and to equality and mutual respect among states.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The PRC Constitution preamble describes the people's democratic dictatorship led by the working class as in essence the dictatorship of the proletariat and does not frame it as lasting only until classes disappear.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The PRC Constitution (Art. 79) fixes indirect election of the President by the National People's Congress.

elective-rulers.rationale: The PRC Constitution (Art. 79) has the President elected by the National People's Congress.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The 20th Congress report says to develop nuclear power in an active, safe and orderly manner.

filial-duty.rationale: The PRC Constitution (Art. 49) states that adult children have the duty to support and assist their parents.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The 20th Congress report says China will never promise to renounce the use of force against separatists seeking Taiwan independence and outside interference.

foreign-policy-non-interference.rationale: The Party Constitution bases China's relations with other countries on mutual noninterference in internal affairs, among the five principles of peaceful coexistence.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Both constitutions make distribution according to work dominant while diverse modes of distribution coexist.

indirect-election.rationale: The PRC Constitution (Arts. 3, 62, 79, 101) has people's congress delegates elect the officials at higher and local levels, and all state organs are created by the congresses.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The Party's standing principle of mutual noninterference in internal affairs is incompatible with great powers sending troops into allied states against their governments.

leader-cult.rationale: The Party Constitution says the Party proscribes all forms of personality cult.

legal-duty-to-work.rationale: The PRC Constitution (Art. 42) states that citizens have the right and the duty to work.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: This is the doctrine's defining formula: the Party and PRC constitutions put the socialist market economy under the Party's leadership.

minority-language-support.rationale: The PRC Constitution (Arts. 4, 121) gives all ethnicities the freedom to use and develop their own languages and has autonomous organs use local languages in their work.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The PRC Constitution (Art. 4) practises regional autonomy where minority ethnicities live in concentrated communities, and the Party Constitution upholds the system of regional ethnic autonomy.

multipolar-world.rationale: The 2021 Resolution records that the Party promoted the development of a multipolar world and took a stand against hegemonism.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The PRC Constitution (Art. 119) has the organs of self-government of ethnic autonomous areas independently administer educational, scientific and cultural affairs in their areas.

national-resource-control.rationale: The PRC Constitution (Art. 9) states that mineral resources, waters, forests and other natural resources are owned by the state, that is, by the whole people.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The Party Constitution calls the realization of communism the Party's highest ideal and ultimate goal.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The PRC Constitution gives the state a leading economic role (Arts. 7, 15), macro-regulation and a social security system (Art. 14).

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The PRC Constitution (Art. 36) bars anyone from using religion to interfere with the educational system of the State.

no-transition-to-communism.rationale: The Party Constitution says China is in the primary stage of socialism, a stage of history that cannot be bypassed, with communism the ultimate goal.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The PRC Constitution (Art. 3) has the congresses constituted through democratic elections, leaving no place for lotteries replacing them.

one-party-rule.rationale: The PRC Constitution (Art. 1) states that the defining feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics is the leadership of the Communist Party, and the Party Constitution puts the Party's leadership over all areas of work.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The PRC Constitution (Art. 57) makes the National People's Congress the highest organ of state power, with the Party leading it.

party-commands-army.rationale: The Party Constitution and the 20th Congress report both require the Party's absolute leadership over the People's Liberation Army and other armed forces.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The Party Constitution's principles of democratic centralism require individual members to defer to Party organizations, the minority to the majority and lower organizations to higher ones.

party-own-road.rationale: The Party Constitution has the Party develop relations with other countries' communist parties on the principles of independence, complete equality, mutual respect and noninterference in each other's internal affairs.

patriotic-education.rationale: The PRC Constitution (Art. 24) has the state conduct education among the people in patriotism.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The PRC Constitution (Art. 128) makes the people's courts the adjudicatory organs of the state.

public-ownership.rationale: The PRC Constitution (Art. 6) makes socialist public ownership of the means of production the basis of the economic system, with the state-owned economy the leading force (Art. 7); the Party Constitution makes public ownership the mainstay.

racial-franchise.rationale: The PRC Constitution (Art. 34) gives every citizen aged 18 the vote regardless of ethnicity or race.

recall-officials.rationale: The PRC Constitution (Art. 77) gives electoral units the power to remove the delegates they elected under legal procedures.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The Party Constitution, the 20th Congress report and the 2021 Resolution all uphold One Country, Two Systems for Hong Kong and Macao, under which those regions keep their own economic and social system.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The 2021 Resolution says the Party worked for a fair and equitable new international political and economic order serving developing countries' interests; the report calls for fairer global governance.

rich-first.rationale: The Party Constitution says that some regions and people may become well-off first.

right-to-secede.rationale: The PRC Constitution (Art. 4) calls all ethnic autonomous areas integral parts of the country and prohibits any act that instigates division; the report opposes separatism.

separated-powers.rationale: The 2021 Resolution calls for guarding against the erosive influence of Western trends of thought, naming separation of powers among them.

social-market-economy.rationale: The PRC Constitution practises a socialist market economy (Art. 15) and a sound social security system (Art. 14).

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The PRC Constitution (Art. 1) calls the state a people's democratic dictatorship led by the working class.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The PRC Constitution (Art. 36) forbids compelling citizens to believe in or not to believe in any religion.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The 20th Congress report says religions in China must be Chinese in orientation and be given active guidance so that they can adapt to socialist society.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The PRC Constitution as amended in 2018 (Art. 79) sets the President's term as the same as the National People's Congress's, with no limit on consecutive terms.

vanguard-party.rationale: The Party Constitution defines the Party as the vanguard of the Chinese working class, the Chinese people and the Chinese nation, and the leadership core of the cause.

women-suffrage.rationale: The PRC Constitution (Art. 34) gives every citizen aged 18 the right to vote and stand for election regardless of sex, and (Art. 48) equal rights for women in political life.

worker-farmer-alliance.rationale: The PRC Constitution (Art. 1) and the 20th Congress report describe the state as led by the working class and based on the alliance of workers and peasants.

workers-councils.rationale: The PRC Constitution (Arts. 2, 3) makes the National People's Congress and local people's congresses the organs of state power, not workers' councils.
